evidence.thread_resolution:
Clem-Fern: Oh yeah i can see your point! In that case, wouldn't that be more adequate to create two distinct options :

- Close the tab on session end => only when explicitly terminated (default and actual behaviour) / always / no

- For Serial, Telnet and SSH, automatically reconnect => yes/no *(locked if tabs are always closed on session end)*
(do not try to reconnect if the session has been manually closed even if yes selected)

It would probably be a good comprise for those who want to keep a way to scroll in the log after the session has been terminated (manually or not) and those who want the tabs to close when the connection is lost.
Eugeny: What if we do it the same way iTerm does it with three options (close / keep / reconnect) + a new one ("auto") where `exit` / Ctrl-D is "close" and otherwise "keep"?

And if you implement this on a profile level, then it's possible to set sensible defaults for each session type (close for local, auto for others)
Clem-Fern: Ok let's do this !
